events.content:
Done — the build passes. I added the custom fonts to `app/BlogHeader.tsx` using Next.js's `next/font/google`: - **Playfair Display** (weight 700) is loaded and applied to the `

` main heading via `playfairDisplay.className`. - **Roboto** (weight 400) is loaded and applied to the `

` subtitle via `roboto.className`. Everything — the font imports, loader calls, and class application — lives entirely inside `BlogHeader.tsx`, so no changes were needed to the layout or global CSS. Using `next/font` means the fonts are self-hosted at build time (no runtime request to Google) and get `font-display: swap` handling automatically to avoid layout shift.

content.text:
Done — the build passes. I added the custom fonts to `app/BlogHeader.tsx` using Next.js's `next/font/google`: - **Playfair Display** (weight 700) is loaded and applied to the `

` main heading via `playfairDisplay.className`. - **Roboto** (weight 400) is loaded and applied to the `

` subtitle via `roboto.className`. Everything — the font imports, loader calls, and class application — lives entirely inside `BlogHeader.tsx`, so no changes were needed to the layout or global CSS. Using `next/font` means the fonts are self-hosted at build time (no runtime request to Google) and get `font-display: swap` handling automatically to avoid layout shift.
